title: 2026-11-12_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_288
description: Investigate and contain the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor compromise in your network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target host in your network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using their Fysbis Linux backdoor. This modular malware establishes command and control (C2) channels, performs lateral movement, and exfiltrates data. Your task is to investigate and contain this threat. Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the training.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: The target host is exhibiting unusual network behavior. Investigate the running services and identify the service name responsible for this suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```

2. List all services, including inactive ones, to identify suspicious services.
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```

3. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay special attention to services with misspellings or unfamiliar descriptions.

4. Identify the suspicious service name: `systemkernelservicedefender.service`

hints.title: Use systemctl to list all services
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.title: Look for unusual services
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay special attention to services with misspellings or unfamiliar descriptions.

hints.title: Search for specific keywords
hints.content: Search for keywords like 'kernel', 'defender', or 'service' in the service names and descriptions.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication. Investigate the service and determine the port number associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL_1 using the `systemctl cat` command.
   ```bash
   systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
   ```

2. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration, which specifies the command launched by the service. This line will contain the port number as an argument.
   ```bash
   ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/ncat -lk 80 -c "cat /var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log" >> /var/log/lab-checkin.log 2>&1'
   ```

3. Identify the port number: `80`

hints.title: Inspect the service configuration
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Find the ExecStart line
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration. The port number is specified as an argument in this line.

hints.title: Extract the port number
hints.content: The port number is the numeric value following the `-lk` argument in the `ExecStart` line.

levels.title: Suspicious File Discovery
levels.content: Investigation indicates that an unauthorized component is executing files on the compromised host. Identify the file path responsible for collecting system information.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL_1 using the `systemctl cat` command.
   ```bash
   systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
   ```

2. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration, which specifies the command launched by the service. This line will contain the file path being executed.
   ```bash
   ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/ncat -lk 80 -c "cat /var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log" >> /var/log/lab-checkin.log 2>&1'
   ```

3. Identify the file path being executed: `/var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log`
